M113 · 2023-12-02 · Renormalization · historical evidence A

An exact RG toy flow and an invariant local exponent

Classical result developed and example checked

The beta function must be specified before discussing running couplings. Simple autonomous flows can be solved exactly, and the derivative at a fixed point gives a local quantity that survives smooth invertible reparametrization of the coupling.

Definitions and assumptions

Write t=log(μ/μ₀) and dg/dt=β(g). A fixed point g* satisfies β(g*)=0.

A scheme coordinate change is a smooth locally invertible h=h(g). Its beta function is β_h(h(g))=h′(g)β(g). This is a coordinate statement for an exact flow, not a guarantee about truncated calculations. The nonzero-initial-condition formula below assumes g₀≠0; g₀=0 is the constant equilibrium.

Flow solutions and fixed-point linearization

For β=bg², g(t)=g₀/(1−bg₀t). For β=−εg+bg² with ε,b>0 and g*=ε/b, g(t)=g*/[1+(g*/g₀−1)e^(εt)] wherever its denominator is nonzero. At a fixed point, dβ_h/dh=β′(g*).

Derivation or proof

The first solution follows by differentiating 1/g. For the second, substitution or separation of variables verifies the displayed logistic-type formula. Linearization gives δġ=β′(g*)δg. Differentiating β_h=h′β with respect to h yields (h″β+h′β′)/h′. At a fixed point β=0, so the derivative equals β′. Thus the local exponent is invariant under the declared regular change of variable, although the numerical coordinate used to label the fixed point can change.

Worked example

Take ε=b=1 and g₀=1/2.

Then g(t)=1/(1+e^t). It approaches the Gaussian fixed point zero as μ increases and the nonzero fixed point one as μ decreases. The derivatives are β′(0)=−1 and β′(1)=1, giving the stated ultraviolet and infrared stability directions. For β=g² with g₀=1/2, the toy solution has a pole at t=2.

These statements are exact for the selected differential equations. A pole in a one-loop approximation does not prove that an underlying physical theory has an actual singularity there; it marks where the approximation can no longer justify extrapolation.

Scope of the result

A field-theoretic beta function depends on the specified action, regulator, renormalization prescription and perturbative order. Multiple couplings require a Jacobian matrix, and marginal directions require nonlinear analysis. An arbitrary scalar cost function is not automatically an RG flow.

Further development

For a specified two-coupling beta vector field, solve the fixed-point equations, classify its Jacobian and compare the invariant eigenvalues under an explicit analytic coordinate change. Report the truncation order with every numerical prediction.

M114 · 2023-12-16 · Analysis · historical evidence A

Moving level sets and the singularity of threshold coordinates

Classical result developed and example checked

An implicit boundary can be differentiated only where its defining level is regular. The same calculation quantifies sensitivity and gives an exact example where a boundary is born and its graph velocity diverges.

Definitions and assumptions

Let f(x,t) be continuously differentiable and consider the level set f(x,t)=c. A regular spatial level has ∇ₓf≠0.

For a one-dimensional graph r(t), the condition is f_r(r(t),t)≠0. Choose the unit normal n=∇f/|∇f| when discussing normal velocity.

Implicit velocity and perturbation sensitivity

Along a regular graph r′=−f_t/f_r. In several dimensions a moving level set has normal velocity v_n=−f_t/|∇f|. A small additive level perturbation δf produces first-order normal displacement −δf/|∇f|.

Derivation or proof

Differentiate f(r(t),t)=c to obtain f_r r′+f_t=0. For a path X(t) on a spatial level, ∇f·X′+f_t=0; taking the normal component gives the velocity. For the perturbation, Taylor-expand f(X+δr n,t)+δf=c and use ∇f·n=|∇f|. The denominator therefore measures conditioning as well as existence of the local graph. Tangential motion is a parametrization choice and is not fixed by the level equation.

Worked example

Take f(x,y,t)=x²+y²−t and c=0.

For t>0 the boundary is a circle of radius sqrt(t), and its outward normal speed is 1/(2sqrt(t)). At t=0 the spatial gradient vanishes at the origin. For t<0 there is no real level set, at zero there is one point, and for t>0 there is a circle. The one-dimensional version r²−t=0 has two branches ±sqrt(t), neither a differentiable graph through the critical event.

The diverging speed is not a contradiction in the implicit-function theorem; it occurs exactly where its nonzero-gradient hypothesis fails. The same inverse-gradient factor explains why threshold localization becomes unstable near a flat or critical level.

Scope of the result

These are local regularity and first-order sensitivity statements. They do not guarantee a global graph, a unique topology, or robustness under large perturbations. Nonsmooth defining functions need generalized notions of normal and solution.

Further development

For a specified smooth family, locate critical levels by solving f=c and ∇f=0 simultaneously, classify the local Hessian, and track which topology changes are compatible with those critical events.

d supplementS008Every channel appears in an inclusion-minimal feasible panelpassThe complete inclusion-minimal panel list is included; no channel was added solely to reach the six-channel count.
d supplementS008Declared greedy heuristic replaypassThe ratio-maximizing heuristic uniquely chooses D (2/3), then F (1/4), then C (1/6), yielding cost16. There are no maximizing ties on this path.
d supplementS008Strict finite greedy gappassGreedy has cost16 versus exact cost13: additive gap3 and ratio16/13 for this constructed declared family only.
d supplementS008Robust lower bounds are attainedpassFive integer perturbations and one exact quadratic-surd perturbation of norm1 attain the stated robust bounds. Each attainer is represented exactly in the certificate.
d supplementS008Withheld-direction exact blindnesspassThe withheld shift2e_D has zero selected mean in A,E, so its observation law equals the null law exactly. Full and greedy panels retain center noncentrality4 and worst-case1 at ε=1.
d supplementS008Projection identitypassThe optimum projection is diag(1,0,0,0,1,0), idempotent with rank2. It has a four-dimensional nullspace, as rank-nullity requires.
eM078Whitened discrepancy and unit invariancepassedr=(1,2), covariance diag(1,4): raw score 5, whitened score 2; rescaling observations and covariance together preserves 2.
eM079Composite derivativepassedAnalytic product gives (5e,e); symmetric finite differences agree within 1e-7.
eM080Graph heat time-step thresholdpassedFour-cycle top mode has λ=4; η=2/5 contracts by −3/5 whereas η=3/5 amplifies by −7/5. Mass is unchanged.
eM081Certified mantissa bracketpassedExact rational squares bracket √5 between 2.2360679774997896964 and 2.2360679774997896965; exponent is exactly 27002.
eM082Noiseless power-family identificationpassedInputs 1,2 identify a=3,b=2; the unused third input x=4 predicts 48 exactly.
eM083Signed dyadic decompositionpasseddiag(−2,0,3) is the sum of two signed rank-one dyads and has a negative quadratic direction, excluding positive-dyad decomposition.
eM084Directional cancellation illustrationpassedAll 225 tangent differences vanish; 15 of 240 horizontal differences are nonzero. This checks only the declared finite directional illustration, not a full transform benchmark.
eM085Normalized qubit kernel reconstructionpassedThe six-axis spherical quadrature reconstructs a nontrivial Hermitian density matrix to <1e-14 and checks normalization and a trace pairing.
eM086Exact polynomial Moyal algebrapassedGaussian rational arithmetic checks q⋆p−p⋆q=i, the full q²⋆p² formula, and all 216 associativity triples from monomials of total degree ≤2. ℏ=1.
eM087Fractional periodic spectral evolutionpassedThree-mode spectral norm and a 16-point physical-space Parseval sum remain one to <1e-14 for α=3/2.
eM088Lagrange identitypassedVectors (1,2,3),(2,−1,4) give Cauchy–Schwarz deficit 150 and squared minors 25+4+121=150.
eM089Winding and sphere calibrationpassedThe analytic derivative ratio for e^(3it) integrates to winding three; curvature×area for radius-two sphere is 4π.
eM090Marked torus stretchpassedThe affine b=2 stretch gives exact Beltrami coefficient −1/3 and dilatation 2; its lattice periods are 1 and 2i.
eM091Certified logistic thresholdspassedExact rational squaring brackets r₂=1+√6 to width 1e−15. Exact rational multipliers at r=3.2 and 3.5 check opposite sides of stability. A two-cycle is checked independently; a numerical derivative/Schwarzian cross-check verifies the flip cubic formula, whose strict positivity is proved analytically in the text.
eM092State-versus-parameter examplespassedExact quadratic critical orbits distinguish c=0,−1,1. Lorenz divergence at σ=10,β=8/3 is −41/3; this is not a chaos certificate.
eM093Convex conjugate and boundary optimizerpassedFor k=2,p=−4 the full-line optimizer is −1 with value 2; the constrained half-line optimizer is 0 with value 0. Fenchel inequalities are checked on rational examples.
eM094CHSH deterministic exhaustionpassedAll sixteen deterministic assignments give S=±2. The declared iid 1000-trial 0.80 win-fraction Hoeffding bound is e^(−5).
eM095Syzygy and strict-transform checkspassedExact polynomial arithmetic verifies both syzygies and generated relations for (x²,xy,y²). The cusp strict transform is v²−x, with derivative −1 in x; its further normal-crossings issue is retained in the text.
eM096Toric lattice certificatepassedThe original determinant is 2; both subdivided cone determinants are 1. Dual Hilbert-generator relation gives uw=v².
eM097Hodge consistency examplespassedKünneth multiplication gives Hodge polynomial (1+uv)² for P¹×P¹. The plane-quintic genus is six and curve Euler characteristic −10.
eM098Conic parametrization and obstructionpassedRational circle parametrizations are checked exactly. Exhaustion modulo three shows a²+b²≡0 forces a≡b≡0, the key step in the primitive descent excluding x²+y²=3 over Q.
eM099Typed composition and Hermitian positivitypassedThe valid derivative product is [2,3,23]. For z=(1,i), zᵀz=0 but z†z=2.
e supplementS012Nontrivial output-quotient counterexamplepassedQ=diag(2,0,3), two-output B: Penrose equations, primal feasibility, stationarity and dual equality all exact. Correct energy 3/5; naive pseudoinverse value 1. Independent one-variable elimination agrees.

e supplementS012Degenerate optimizer setspassedSample points on the exact rank-one optimal segments/rays and the a=0 null-coordinate family remain feasible with the stated energy. Full optimizer-set formulas are proved in the text.
e independentS014Independent quartic complete Jordan certificatepassedExact Q(i) pair-site reconstruction of all four Hamiltonians, jet basis rank4, full operator reconstruction and common nilpotent ranks2,1,0.
e independentS014Independent eight-site characteristic polynomial by determinantspassedNine exact Gaussian-rational determinant evaluations prove the degree-eight factorization independently of the producer’s Newton/trace algorithm. Full values retained in this certificate.
fM100Bernstein–Sato coefficient identitiespassedExact rational coefficient equality for x^m, m=1,…,8, and x²y³; the quadratic Laplacian coefficient is 4(s+1)². Minimality is proved in the entry by normal-order exponent comparison.
fM101Conic polarity and tangent-locus testpassedQp=(2,0,−1); Q⁻¹(Qp)=p. A rational point satisfies its tangent equation. The polar of the exterior point has dual quadratic value 3 and is not itself tangent.
fM102Ordered cross-ratio under a projectivitypassedThe homogeneous tuple (−1,1;0,∞) has cross-ratio −1 before and after the determinant-one map z↦(2z+3)/(z+2).
fM103Heisenberg mode algebra on polynomial statespassedAll 162 mixed-mode commutators tested equal mδ_mn on the selected monomials. L₂L₋₂ applied to the vacuum is exactly 1/2, giving c=1 in the stated Virasoro convention. These finite checks accompany, not replace, the formal proof.
fM104Four-site XXX spectrum and Bethe rootspassedThe integer one-magnon Hamiltonian has a checked eigenbasis with energies 0,2,2,4. The three finite rapidities satisfy the one-root periodic Bethe equation and match the nonuniform-state energies; the uniform state is the infinite-root limit.
fM105Gaudin matrices and exact oper residual polynomialspassedThe singlet and triplet Ω eigenvalues are verified with rational matrices. The polynomial 4g²(1+D′)−3D² is identically zero, proving V=3/(4g²), not merely sampling it. Both scaled solution residual polynomials vanish identically, and their Wronskian is exactly one. Full coefficient certificate is included.
fM105Complete rational three-site Gaudin spectrum and operspassedFor z=(0,1,8/3), roots 2 and4/9 produce two joint doublets; the vacuum family supplies a quartet. Eight explicit rational eigenvectors have rank8 and all three full Hamiltonians commute. Both Miura potential identities have exactly zero cross-multiplied residual polynomials, proving apparent-pole cancellation and residue/eigenvalue agreement.
fM106Independence arithmetic and dependence boundspassedThe exact rational product is approximately 0.00482230805327. Fréchet bounds from the 104 marginals are [0,0.95]. Enumerating the four XOR outcomes verifies pairwise independence while the three-way all-one event has probability zero.
fM107Nonlinear observation collisionpassedFor both initial states ±1, y(t)=1/(1+2t) satisfies y′=−2y² exactly at rational test times; the entry proves the full formula and convergence, so the sign collision holds for the entire time history.
fM108Klein–Gordon dispersion residualpassedFor c=ℏ=1,m=2,k=(3,0,0),ω²=13 gives the exact polynomial residual −13+9+4=0. The general dispersion is derived directly in the entry.
fM109Pauli algebra and nonrelativistic energy expansionpassedExact small-matrix products verify σ₁σ₂=iσ₃ and σᵢ²=I. The squared truncated polynomial (1+x/2−x²/8)² agrees with 1+x through x². The entry derives the magnetic sign from the covariant-momentum commutator.
fM110Exterior derivative and plane-wave checkspassedThe mixed second-derivative coefficients cancel in d²χ and dF for the stated potential, while the vacuum dispersion residual ω²−k² vanishes. The proof uses d²=0 and states the local/global potential distinction.
fM111Ward difference identity and transverse null directionpassedThe longitudinal vertex obeys the matrix-valued difference identity exactly for rational momenta in a two-dimensional Euclidean Clifford example. A separately constructed nonzero transverse term contracts to zero.
fM112Gaussian quartic perturbation coefficientspassedGaussian-moment recurrence gives Z=1−g/8+35g²/384+… and normalized G₂=1−g/2+2g²/3+…. Connected logZ has second coefficient 1/12. The coefficient ratio grows asymptotically as 2n/3; the entry provides a finite-order remainder bound rather than claiming convergence.
fM113Toy beta flow and fixed-point slopespassedg(t)=1/(1+e^t) satisfies β=−g+g² to numerical roundoff at sample times; β′(0)=−1 and β′(1)=1 are exact. The entry proves the formula and coordinate-invariance of fixed-point linearization.
fM114Regular-level velocity and critical-level failurepassedFor radii 1,2,3 at t=1,4,9, the exact differentiated constraint 2rr′−1=0 holds. At t=0 the spatial gradient is zero, exactly violating the regular-level assumption; the entry proves the general normal-velocity formula.
f supplementS010Complete rational 2-site one-magnon sectorpassedExact matrices, orthogonal eigenbasis, projector resolution of identity and all Hamiltonian reconstructions passed. Every critical-root scalar equation has a zero potential residual, two zero ODE residuals and Wronskian one.
f supplementS010Complete rational 3-site one-magnon sectorpassedExact matrices, orthogonal eigenbasis, projector resolution of identity and all Hamiltonian reconstructions passed. Every critical-root scalar equation has a zero potential residual, two zero ODE residuals and Wronskian one.
f supplementS010Complete rational 4-site one-magnon sectorpassedExact matrices, orthogonal eigenbasis, projector resolution of identity and all Hamiltonian reconstructions passed. Every critical-root scalar equation has a zero potential residual, two zero ODE residuals and Wronskian one.
f supplementS010Exact exceptional three-site Jordan pointpassedIn Q(tau), tau²−tau+1=0, the two critical roots coalesce. B=B′=0, each generalized-eigenvector equation holds with a nonzero coefficient, and (u,v,v′) has rank3. Hamiltonians commute; the surviving scalar equation retains zero residuals and Wronskian1.
f supplementS010Independent replay of the full eight-dimensional rational examplepassedRead the published rational 8×8 matrices and all eight vectors from the separate certificate, recomputed all joint eigenvector equations, and verified rank8. This independently replays the quartet plus two doublets certificate.
f spectralS013Exceptional Gram and constant-projector identitiespassedIn Q(tau), both v and v′ are bilinearly isotropic, vᵀv′=−3/p0, and Q=−p0(v′vᵀ+vv′ᵀ)/3 exactly. Q²=Q; the nonzero leading divergence coefficient C=−p0vvᵀ/2 satisfies C²=0.
f spectralS013All three exact nonzero square-zero Jordan partspassedEach N_i=(H_i−E_i)Q equals (p0 a_i²/3)vvᵀ, is nonzero, has square zero and is supported on Q. The differentiated generalized-eigenvector identities hold, proving a size-two block for every H_i on the highest-weight plane.
f spectralS013Projector blowup with bounded sumpassedComplex sample approaches satisfy the exact projector formula, show ε||P+|| tending to a nonzero coefficient and cancellation P++P−=Q to roundoff. This numerical illustration accompanies the analytic |D|^(−1/2) proof.
f spectralS013Tracked spectral-cover label exchangepassedA small loop around one discriminant root flips the continued square root and exchanges w+ with w−. This is a label-continuation calculation, not KZ parallel transport; the proof uses the winding of D.
f jordanS014Multiplicity-three critical point and complete length-three chainpassedFor sites (1,−1,i,−i), all four Hamiltonians satisfy the exact Taylor-chain polynomial relations. The uniform vector plus V₀,V₁,V₂ has rank4. On the highest-weight plane N²≠0 and N³=0; the full characteristic polynomial is (λ−3/4)(λ+1/4)³.
f jordanS014Closed characteristic formula and fractional-linear Hamiltonian identities for four sitespassedExact Gaussian-rational evaluation verifies χ_Hi(λ)=u^n p′(z_i+1/u)/p′(z_i) at the base site. All A_j[I+(z_i−z_j)A_i]=A_i identities hold with invertible denominators.
f jordanS014Mixed multiplicity example with exact characteristic factorizationpassedFor eight sites ±1,±i,±2,±2i, the multiplicity-three chain is checked for every Hamiltonian. An independent Newton/trace computation of the full H₁ characteristic polynomial exactly matches the stated cubic factor times four distinct regular-root factors and the uniform factor. All Hamiltonians commute.
f jordanS014Closed characteristic formula and fractional-linear identities in the mixed casepassedThe general characteristic-polynomial formula independently reproduces the full degree-eight polynomial, and all eight Hamiltonian fractional-linear relations have exactly invertible denominators and zero residual matrices.
